A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VQ-FocusAmbiguity and its recognition and localization tasks, despite the title changing from Accounting to Acknowledging Focus Ambiguity in Visual Questions. Both main texts and complete appendices, including figures and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, recognition experiments with GPT-4o and InternVL2, localization experiments, and supplementary qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses and reports additional model comparisons, prompt experiments, model-size and fine-tuning studies, and input ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 adds an engineered Molmo+SAM localization procedure: Molmo predicts points for plausible focus regions, which SAM converts into segmentations. This introduces a distinct inference pipeline alongside the retained direct GLaMM and GPT-4o-description-to-GLaMM approaches.

E1.justification: The four source datasets and two principal tasks remain the same; increased sample counts do not constitute new coverage. However, v2 Section 9.3 adds recognition scenarios with the image withheld or replaced by a generated caption, extending evaluation to limited new input conditions.

E2.justification: The main recognition comparison expands from GPT-4o and InternVL2 to also include Qwen2.5-VL and Molmo; the appendix adds ChatGPT-o3 results. Localization adds Molmo+SAM. The earlier End-to-End and Multi-Step approaches remain as GLaMM and GPT-4o+GLaMM, respectively.

E3.justification: The reported dataset grows from 4,357 to 5,500 examples and the test split from 4,217 to 5,360, while training and validation retain 70 examples each. Recognition replaces weighted precision and recall with positive rate. The stated InternVL2 configuration changes from Pro to Llama3-76B, and enhanced-CoT instructions add a plural-form exception. New experiments introduce model-size, fine-tuning, and input-modality conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds prompt-definition ablations, Qwen2.5-VL size comparisons and fine-tuning, GPT-4o question-only and caption-input ablations, and recognition success/failure cases in Sections 9.2–9.3. It also adds Molmo+SAM failure examples. The earlier recognition breakdowns by ambiguity label and source-specific F1 are omitted, while the existing grounding analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated benchmark runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. v2's additional question-length standard deviations describe dataset dispersion rather than introducing uncertainty estimation for model results.

E6.justification: Recognition scores and rankings change substantially: Table 2's highest accuracy is 54.4% for InternVL2 ZS-ECoT in v1 and 69.6% for GPT-4o ZS-CoT in v2. These are revised-setting results, not controlled performance gains. New results include Molmo+SAM's 24.3 mAP and ChatGPT-o3's 70.9% FS-ECoT accuracy. The original localization rows in Table 3 and grounding-agreement counts in Table 4 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, assumptions, propositions, or proofs. The localization metric definitions are retained; expanded conceptual explanations and prompt instructions do not introduce mathematical results.

C1.justification: The novelty claim is qualified from being the first dataset locating question content toward being the first dataset specifically organized around focus ambiguity, alongside acknowledgment of earlier question grounding. The central contributions remain the dataset, two benchmark tasks, and evidence that current models struggle.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the interpretation of recognition behavior, adding hypotheses about counting/pointing pretraining, reasoning prompts, few-shot bias, visual dependence, and abstention. It also explains new localization limitations, including SAM's incomplete object segmentation and Molmo's failure with long FS-ECoT inputs. These extend beyond the earlier discussion of missed regions and question-versus-answer confusion.

D1.justification: v2 specifies model checkpoints in Section 9.1 and substantially expands prompt documentation in Figures 18–22, including the previously omitted full ambiguity definition and explicit FS-ECoT reasoning. It adds annotation-rule development details and localization output-format instructions. The advertised dataset/evaluation-server address changes, while the earlier code address remains. Training details for the new fine-tuning experiment are still missing.

R1.justification: The related-work framework remains, but v2 adds Visual7W and explicitly distinguishes prior question grounding from its focus-ambiguity contribution. It also adds literature supporting the zero/few-shot design and the newly evaluated models, while removing the earlier Eppler visual-ambiguity citation. These are targeted positioning refinements rather than a wholesale literature reorganization.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and author-contribution edits, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, motivation, dataset description, and benchmarking narrative. It consolidates the earlier Model Design and Model Analysis appendix sections into a structured Section 9 and repairs conspicuous malformed sentences and headings in v1.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns Figure 1, merges the question-length and initial-word displays into Figure 2, restructures the recognition plots, and expands the localization figure. Table 2 changes both model rows and metric columns. New displays include the interaction-interface illustration, prompt boxes, Tables 5–6, and qualitative cases. Existing annotation screenshots and grounding examples are largely retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the narrow empirical foundation of v1 through broader model comparisons and diagnostic controls examining prompt wording, model size, fine-tuning, and dependence on visual input. Its fuller prompt specifications address an important reproducibility gap, and acknowledging Visual7W makes the novelty positioning more precise. The new fine-tuning experiment remains underdocumented, and revised settings prevent interpreting cross-version scores as controlled gains, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvements in empirical support and clarity.
